---
title: "Loading your data"
subtitle: "Supported input formats, their file layout, the reader function and its return value"
aliases:
  - ../guide/loading.html
---

FALCONAge scores data that is already preprocessed and quality controlled. Normalisation,
detection filtering and sample QC of methylation arrays belong upstream, in an array
pipeline such as [methylarray](https://github.com/bhagesh-h/methylarray), minfi or SeSAMe;
FALCONAge takes their beta matrix as input. Clinical chemistry and NMR tables are read as
reported by the laboratory.

Every reader returns a `FalconData`: a samples-by-features matrix with its modality,
platform and sample annotation. Scoring is the same call whichever reader produced it.

Every output on this page was produced by running the code above it, against the public
test corpus where the corpus has that input type and against a small file written inline
where it does not. Nothing here is illustrative.

## Readers by input format

| Input | Reader | Modality | CLI |
|---|---|---|---|
| A beta matrix: CSV, TSV, parquet or `.h5ad` | `read_betas()` | `dna_methylation` | `falconage run betas.csv` |
| A GEO series matrix | `read_series_matrix()` | `dna_methylation` | `falconage run GSE…_series_matrix.txt.gz` |
| A ComputAgeBench study | `read_computage_bench()` | `dna_methylation` | |
| A targeted assay: pyrosequencing, EpiTYPER, ddPCR | `read_panel()` | `dna_methylation` | |
| Clinical chemistry | `read_clinical()` | `clinical_chemistry` | `falconage run labs.csv --kind clinical` |
| Nightingale NMR metabolomics | `read_nightingale()` | `metabolomics_nmr` | `falconage run nmr.xlsx --kind nightingale` |

Raw IDAT files, sequencing coverage files (RRBS, bedMethyl) and proteomic or
transcriptomic tables are not accepted. A folder of IDATs passed to `falconage run` is
refused with a message naming the preprocessing step it needs.

`fa.read(path)` selects the reader from the file name. Arguments specific to a reader,
such as the units of a clinical table, are passed to that reader directly.

## A beta matrix

Probes down the rows, samples across the columns, or the transpose: the orientation is
detected from which axis carries probe ids.

```python
d = fa.read_betas("betas.csv")
```

```
FalconData(3 samples x 3 features, dna_methylation, 0.0% missing)
```

The file that produced it:

```
probe,S001,S002,S003
cg00000029,0.512,0.488,0.559
cg00000165,0.113,0.096,0.140
cg00000236,0.842,0.871,0.836
```

Betas belong in 0 to 1. A matrix of percentages is a factor of a hundred out and every
clock will return a confidently wrong number, so `prepare()` checks the range and says so.

**EPIC v2 identifiers are harmonised automatically.** EPIC v2 probe ids carry a suffix
(`cg00000029_TC21`), and a clock fitted on 450K finds no matching features until the
suffixes are removed. `prepare()` removes them and averages replicate probes of the same
CpG; `aggregate_epicv2=False` disables the step.

**Pass the matrix before probe filtering.** Filters for SNP, cross-reactive or
detection-failed probes are designed for association studies. A clock CpG removed by them
is replaced by an imputed value at scoring time, and `score()` reports how much of each
clock's weight that affects (see [Preparing data and coverage](preprocessing.qmd)).

## A GEO series matrix

The `*_series_matrix.txt.gz` GEO offers for most published studies. Sample metadata
comes with it.

```python
d = fa.read_series_matrix("GSE330325_series_matrix.txt.gz")
d.obs.head(3)
```

```
FalconData(8 samples x 888987 features, dna_methylation, EPICv2, 0.0% missing)

                 title            tissue    cell_type
sample_id
GSM9723838  GSD1a_rep1  Skin Fibroblasts  Fibroblasts
GSM9723839  GSD1a_rep2  Skin Fibroblasts  Fibroblasts
GSM9723840  GSD1a_rep3  Skin Fibroblasts  Fibroblasts
```

The `characteristics:` lines become `obs` columns. Set `obs["tissue"]` before scoring
and the specimen check runs; leave it and every clock's tissue assumption goes unchecked.

## A ComputAgeBench study

65 curated case-control studies with age, sex, tissue and condition already normalised.

```python
fa.io.list_computage_bench().head()
d = fa.read_computage_bench("GSE107143")
```

```
              n platform tissue      conditions  age_min  age_max
dataset
GSE56046   1128     450K  Blood  AS=789, HC=339     44.0     83.0
GSE42861    689     450K  Blood  HC=335, RA=354     18.0     70.0
GSE117859   608     450K  Blood         HIV=608     25.0     75.0
GSE111629   572     450K  Blood  HC=237, PD=335     35.0     92.0
GSE117860   529   EPICv1  Blood         HIV=529     25.0     75.0

FalconData(16 samples x 460295 features, dna_methylation, 450K, 0.0% missing)

              dataset       gpl tissue    cell_type sex   age condition class
SampleID
GSM2861662  GSE107143  GPL13534  Blood  Whole blood   M  79.0        AS   CVD
GSM2861663  GSE107143  GPL13534  Blood  Whole blood   M  88.0        AS   CVD
GSM2861664  GSE107143  GPL13534  Blood  Whole blood   M  88.0        AS   CVD
```

This is the input `run_benchmark()` expects: it needs `condition`, a control group, and
`age`, and this reader supplies all three.

## A targeted assay

Pyrosequencing, EpiTYPER, ddPCR: a handful of CpGs measured directly, with samples down
the rows.

```python
d = fa.read_panel("panel.csv")
```

```
FalconData(2 samples x 3 features, dna_methylation, targeted panel, 0.0% missing)
```

```
sample,cg16867657,cg09809672,cg02228185
P01,0.68,0.41,0.55
P02,0.72,0.38,0.51
```

A panel almost never carries a whole clock, and the coverage floor is what stops a
three-probe file being scored as though it were a 353-probe model. `probe_loss()` says
what a partial set costs before you score anything.

## Clinical chemistry

The clinical clocks take laboratory values, and they take them in declared units.

```python
UNITS = {"albumin": "g/L", "creatinine": "umol/L", "glucose": "mmol/L",
         "crp": "mg/L", "lymphocyte_percent": "%", "mean_cell_volume": "fL",
         "red_cell_distribution_width": "%", "alkaline_phosphatase": "U/L",
         "white_blood_cell_count": "10^9/L"}

d = fa.read_clinical("labs.csv", units=UNITS)
fa.score(d, clocks=["phenoage"]).scores.round(2)
```

```
FalconData(2 samples x 10 features, clinical_chemistry, 0.0% missing)

WARNING [phenoage] Two constants circulate in the divisor of the Gompertz inversion:
0.090165 and 0.09165. FALCONAge uses 0.090165, the value BioAge corrected to in April
2026. Code still using 0.09165 differs by several years on the same input.

           phenoage
sample_id
C01           55.79
C02           69.61
```

**Units are per column, not per file.** A clinical table mixes them, so there is no single
name to pass; `units="SI"` is refused with the mapping it wants. PhenoAge exists in an SI
and a conventional variant that disagree by years, and `units=` has no default for that
reason.

**HbA1c in mmol/mol.** Laboratories outside the US report HbA1c in IFCC units. Declare
`"hba1c": "mmol/mol"` and it is converted to the NGSP percentage the reference models were
fitted in, by the published master equation NGSP = 0.09148 × IFCC + 2.152
([NGSP](https://ngsp.org/ifccngsp.asp); Hoelzel et al., *Clin Chem* 2004;50:166-174,
[doi:10.1373/clinchem.2003.024802](https://doi.org/10.1373/clinchem.2003.024802)). It is
not a ratio, so it applies to HbA1c only.

**A cohort measured unlike its reference.** KDM and homeostatic dysregulation are fitted on a
reference cohort, and `fit_kdm`/`fit_hd` record each marker's distribution there. When a scored
cohort leaves it, `score()` says so (category `reference_range`): a median outside the
reference's 1st to 99th percentile, which is what a unit mismatch looks like, or many values
beyond the reference's range. The case that matters most is CRP. NHANES III's assay read
nothing below 0.21 mg/dL, and 63.9% of its adults sit at that floor, so a high-sensitivity CRP
cohort scored against it has most of its values where the reference has none.
`fa.models.clinical.censor_to_reference(df, ref)` sets values below a reference's reporting
floor to the floor, which is how the reference itself recorded them, and returns how many
moved. It only touches markers whose minimum is a floor (at least 1% of reference rows sitting
exactly at it); values above the reference's range are real measurements and are left alone.

## NMR metabolomics

A Nightingale Health export (CSV, TSV or Excel), samples down the rows:

```python
d = fa.read_nightingale("nightingale.xlsx")      # Excel needs the `metabolomics` extra (openpyxl)
res = fa.score(d, clocks=["metaboage", "metabohealth"])
```

Column names are translated to the BBMRI-NL names the two scores were fitted with, by MiMIR's
table and MiMIR's rule (lower-cased, and translated only when exactly one entry lists the name);
a name the table does not know is kept and listed in `obs.attrs["untranslated"]` rather than
guessed. MetaboAge (van den Akker et al. 2020) and MetaboHealth (Deelen et al. 2019) are scored as
MiMIR scores them, its quality control included, and match it to 1e-9 and 1e-12. MetaboHealth
z-scores each measure within the cohort, so a score depends on who else is in the file: it is
marked `requires_cohort` and is not comparable between files scored separately.

## After loading

Whatever you loaded, the rest is the same:

```python
res = fa.score(d, clocks="compatible")   # only the clocks this data supports
res.interpretation()                     # scale, unit, legal operations, caveats
fa.technical_se(res, d)                  # how much of each score is the assay
```

`clocks="compatible"` is the safe default: it asks the registry which clocks this
platform, modality and specimen actually support, and skips the rest by name rather than
scoring them on whatever features happen to match.
